The text panel at the top is the authoritative metric contract the .NET side codes against.

options.content:
# Hephaisto — agent telemetry

**This dashboard is the metric spec.** The .NET agent must emit exactly the instruments below.
Names come from `src/Hephaisto.Core/Telemetry/HephaistoTelemetry.Metrics` (OTel dotted form);
the Prometheus names here are what the OTel Collector's `prometheusremotewrite` exporter
produces from them with `add_metric_suffixes: true` (dots → `_`, monotonic sums → `_total`,
UCUM unit appended, `{annotation}` units dropped, histograms → `_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count`).

| OTel instrument | Prometheus name | Type / unit | Labels |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hephaisto.signals.received` | `hephaisto_signals_received_total` | Counter `{signal}` | `source`, `kind`, `severity` |
| `hephaisto.signals.dropped` | `hephaisto_signals_dropped_total` | Counter `{signal}` | `reason` |
| `hephaisto.incidents.opened` | `hephaisto_incidents_opened_total` | Counter `{incident}` | `kind`, `severity` |
| `hephaisto.incidents.closed` | `hephaisto_incidents_closed_total` | Counter `{incident}` | `kind`, `severity`, `outcome` |
| `hephaisto.incidents.open` | `hephaisto_incidents_open` | UpDownCounter `{incident}` | `kind`, `severity` |
| `hephaisto.detection.latency` | `hephaisto_detection_latency_seconds` | **Histogram** `s` — **MTTD** | `kind`, `severity` |
| `hephaisto.incident.duration` | `hephaisto_incident_duration_seconds` | **Histogram** `s` — **MTTR** | `kind`, `outcome` |
| `hephaisto.investigation.duration` | `hephaisto_investigation_duration_seconds` | Histogram `s` | `kind`, `termination_reason` |
| `hephaisto.investigation.steps` | `hephaisto_investigation_steps` | Histogram `{step}` | `kind`, `termination_reason` |
| `hephaisto.investigation.terminations` | `hephaisto_investigation_terminations_total` | Counter `{investigation}` | `reason`, `kind` |
| `hephaisto.tool.calls` | `hephaisto_tool_calls_total` | Counter `{call}` | `tool`, `outcome` |
| `hephaisto.tool.duration` | `hephaisto_tool_duration_seconds` | Histogram `s` | `tool`, `outcome` |
| `hephaisto.llm.tokens` | `hephaisto_llm_tokens_total` | Counter `{token}` | `model`, `token_kind` (`input`/`output`) |
| `hephaisto.llm.cost_usd` | `hephaisto_llm_cost_usd_total` | Counter `{USD}` | `model`, `operation` |
| `hephaisto.llm.budget_utilization` | `hephaisto_llm_budget_utilization` | Gauge `1` (0..1+) | `scope` (`hour-tokens`/`hour-cost`/`day-cost`) |
| `hephaisto.policy.decisions` | `hephaisto_policy_decisions_total` | Counter `{decision}` | `decision`, `reason`, `action_type`, `risk` |
| `hephaisto.actions.executed` | `hephaisto_actions_executed_total` | Counter `{action}` | `action_type`, `outcome`, `mode` |
| `hephaisto.actions.rolled_back` | `hephaisto_actions_rolled_back_total` | Counter `{action}` | `action_type`, `reason` |
| `hephaisto.verification.result` | `hephaisto_verification_result_total` | Counter `{verification}` | `outcome`, `action_type` |
| `hephaisto.grounding.rejected` | `hephaisto_grounding_rejected_total` | Counter `{rejection}` | `reason`, `stage` |
| `hephaisto.budget.remaining` | `hephaisto_budget_remaining` | Gauge `{USD}` | `scope` |
| `hephaisto.mode` | `hephaisto_mode` | Gauge `1` | *(none)* |
| `hephaisto.human.feedback` | `hephaisto_human_feedback_total` | Counter `{verdict}` | `verdict`, `kind` |

### Two contract decisions worth reading

**Mode is an encoded gauge, not an info-metric.** `hephaisto_mode` carries the numeric value of
`Hephaisto.Core.Domain.AgentMode` — `0=Off, 1=Observe, 2=DryRun, 3=Auto` — and every panel that shows it
uses Grafana value mappings, so it reads as the word. There is no `hephaisto_mode_info{mode="..."}`;
do not emit one. A single gauge cannot go stale the way a set of info series can (an info-metric leaves the
previous mode's series at `1` until the exporter forgets it), which is exactly the failure you cannot afford
on a kill switch. The three modes named in the brief map on as `observe → Observe(1)`, `suggest → DryRun(2)`,
`act → Auto(3)`; `Off(0)` is the fourth, real state.

**Label values are the enum member names, verbatim and case-sensitive** — `CrashLoopBackOff`, `RequireApproval`,
`RolloutRestart`, `Concluded`. Queries here match them exactly. Emit `kind` from `SignalKind`, `decision` from
`PolicyDecision`, `action_type` from `ActionType`, `reason` on terminations from `TerminationReason`.
Free-text label values, per-incident ids, or pod names in labels will blow up cardinality — keep them on spans.

`outcome` on actions/verification is the lower-case set `succeeded` / `failed` / `skipped` (+ `inconclusive` for
verification). `verdict` on human feedback is `correct` / `incorrect` / `partial` / `unclear`.

panels.title: Agent mode
panels.description: hephaisto_mode — gauge encoding Hephaisto.Core.Domain.AgentMode (0=Off, 1=Observe, 2=DryRun, 3=Auto). Rendered through value mappings so it reads as the word. This is the kill switch: anything other than ACT means no mutation reaches the cluster. Emit as a single gauge, NOT as hephaisto_mode_info.

panels.title: LLM budget utilization
panels.description: hephaisto_llm_budget_utilization — gauge, 0..1+, labelled by scope (hour-tokens/hour-cost/day-cost). Thresholds mirror the alert rules exactly: HephaistoLlmBudgetWarning fires on >0.8 for 5m (yellow), HephaistoLlmBudgetExhausted on >=1.0 (red). At >=1.0 the agent stops spending and escalates with EscalationReason.BudgetExhausted.

panels.title: Incidents opened / closed by kind
panels.description: rate(hephaisto_incidents_opened_total[$__rate_interval]) and the matching closed counter, both by SignalKind. Opened is drawn solid, closed dashed. A persistent gap between the two is the queue growing — cross-check against 'Incidents open now'.

panels.title: Incidents open now
panels.description: sum(hephaisto_incidents_open) — UpDownCounter, incremented on open and decremented on every terminal transition (Resolved, Escalated, Suppressed, Expired). If this drifts upward forever, a close path is missing a decrement.

panels.title: Open incidents by kind
panels.description: sum by (kind) (hephaisto_incidents_open) — which SignalKind is currently occupying the agent.

panels.title: MTTD (mean over window)
panels.description: MTTD — hephaisto_detection_latency_seconds histogram: signal first seen to incident opened. The stat is a true mean over the dashboard window (increase(_sum[$__range]) / increase(_count[$__range])), not a point-in-time rate ratio.

panels.title: MTTR (mean over window)
panels.description: MTTR — hephaisto_incident_duration_seconds histogram: incident opened to terminal state. Same windowed-mean construction as MTTD. Note this includes escalated incidents, whose clock stops when a human takes over; filter outcome="resolved" for the pure auto-resolve figure.

panels.title: MTTD — mean & p95
panels.description: MTTD — hephaisto_detection_latency_seconds histogram: signal first seen to incident opened. The stat is a true mean over the dashboard window (increase(_sum[$__range]) / increase(_count[$__range])), not a point-in-time rate ratio.

panels.title: MTTR — mean & p95
panels.description: MTTR — hephaisto_incident_duration_seconds histogram: incident opened to terminal state. Same windowed-mean construction as MTTD. Note this includes escalated incidents, whose clock stops when a human takes over; filter outcome="resolved" for the pure auto-resolve figure.

panels.title: Investigation duration (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: hephaisto_investigation_duration_seconds histogram — wall clock of one investigation loop. Suggested bucket boundaries (seconds): 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600, 1200. A p99 pinned to the top bucket usually means WallClockExhausted terminations, not slow tools — check the terminations panel.

panels.title: Investigation steps (avg / p95 / p99)
panels.description: hephaisto_investigation_steps histogram — LLM turns + tool calls per investigation. Suggested buckets: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32. NOTE: a histogram cannot yield a true max; p99 is the honest ceiling and is labelled as such. If a real max is wanted, emit an additional gauge — do not read histogram_quantile(1,...), which returns +Inf whenever the overflow bucket is non-empty.

panels.title: Investigation terminations by reason
panels.description: hephaisto_investigation_terminations_total by TerminationReason. Concluded is the only clean exit; everything else is a budget or fault exit. Concluded is forced green and drawn first, budget exits amber, Faulted/Stalled red.

panels.title: Clean conclusion rate
panels.description: Share of investigations that ended via TerminationReason.Concluded rather than a budget, stall or fault exit — the single best summary of whether the investigation loop is actually working. Falling below ~0.7 means the step/token budgets are too tight for the incidents being handled.

panels.title: LLM spend rate by model (USD / hour)
panels.description: rate(hephaisto_llm_cost_usd_total[$__rate_interval]) * 3600, by model. The counter is monotonic USD, incremented once per completed model call from the provider's reported token usage times the configured price table — never estimated from a tokenizer.

panels.title: Spend this window
panels.description: sum(increase(hephaisto_llm_cost_usd_total[$__range])) — total USD burned across all models over the dashboard's current time range. Follows the time picker, so widening the range widens the figure.

panels.title: Cumulative spend by model (window)
panels.description: sum by (model) (increase(hephaisto_llm_cost_usd_total[$__range])) — which model is eating the budget. Split routing (a cheap triage model, an expensive planning model) shows up here as a wide split.

panels.title: Budget utilization over time (by scope)
panels.description: hephaisto_llm_budget_utilization with the alert thresholds drawn as lines: 0.8 = HephaistoLlmBudgetWarning (>0.8 for 5m), 1.0 = HephaistoLlmBudgetExhausted (>=1.0). Crossing 1.0 halts spending and escalates.

panels.title: Token throughput by model (tokens / sec)
panels.description: hephaisto_llm_tokens_total by model and token_kind (input/output). Output tokens dominating cost while input stays flat is the signature of a runaway reasoning loop.

panels.title: Policy decisions by decision & reason
panels.description: hephaisto_policy_decisions_total by PolicyDecision and reason. The engine is default-deny, so Deny with an empty or generic reason means a rule did not fire — that is a bug, not a safe default. Colour is fixed per decision: Allow green, RequireApproval yellow, Deny red.

panels.title: Policy decisions — window totals
panels.description: sum by (decision, reason) (increase(hephaisto_policy_decisions_total[$__range])) — the same data ranked, for reading off which rule is doing the most work over the window.

panels.title: Actions executed by type & outcome
panels.description: hephaisto_actions_executed_total by ActionType and outcome. Failures are forced red, thick and filled so they are unmissable against the green success bands; succeeded is green, skipped grey.

panels.title: Action failure rate
panels.description: increase(hephaisto_actions_executed_total{outcome="failed"}[$__range]) over all executions. In Observe and DryRun mode this should be flat zero — a non-zero value there means the executor bypassed the mode gate.

panels.title: Rollbacks (window)
panels.description: sum(increase(hephaisto_actions_rolled_back_total[$__range])) — every rollback also escalates with EscalationReason.RollbackPerformed, so any non-zero value here has a matching human-facing incident.

panels.title: Grounding rejections by reason
panels.description: hephaisto_grounding_rejected_total by reason — the agent throwing away its own conclusions because the cited evidence failed the substring check. THIS IS NOT AN ERROR: it is the guardrail working, and is deliberately coloured blue/purple rather than red. What matters is the trend — a sustained rise means prompt drift or a model regression, and should be read next to the clean-conclusion rate.

panels.title: Human feedback verdicts (window)
panels.description: hephaisto_human_feedback_total by verdict — the only honest false-positive signal available, collected from the operator UI. correct/incorrect/partial/unclear.

panels.title: Grounding rejections per investigation
panels.description: increase(hephaisto_grounding_rejected_total[$__range]) / increase(hephaisto_investigation_duration_seconds_count[$__range]). Normalised so it does not simply track investigation volume. A quality signal, not an error rate.

panels.title: Feedback precision
panels.description: correct / (correct + incorrect + partial) from hephaisto_human_feedback_total. 'unclear' is excluded from the denominator on purpose — it is a missing judgement, not a wrong one.

panels.title: Verification pass rate
panels.description: hephaisto_verification_result_total{outcome="passed"} over all verifications — did the action actually fix the thing. 'inconclusive' counts against the rate here, which is intentional: an unverifiable action is not a successful one.

panels.title: Signals dropped (window)
panels.description: sum(increase(hephaisto_signals_dropped_total[$__range])) — ingest-side losses (queue full, unparseable webhook, out-of-scope namespace). Distinct from suppression, which happens after an incident exists.

panels.title: Logs — the agent's own reasoning trace
Log volume by level
panels.description: count_over_time over the agent's own log stream, split by Loki's detected_level. Use this to find the spike, then read the lines below it in the logs panel.

panels.title: Hephaisto agent logs
panels.description: Loki: {k8s_namespace_name="hephaisto", k8s_deployment_name="hephaisto"} filtered by the $search textbox variable (leave it empty to match everything — |= "" is a no-op in LogQL). This is the jump-off point from a metric spike to the reasoning trace: the agent logs one line per investigation step with the incident id, so type an incident GUID into $search to read a single investigation end to end. Trace ids in these lines link into Tempo (uid: tempo) via the Loki datasource's derived field.
